steps.why: Plaster of Paris is useful because of what it does with water. It takes the water back, hardens, and expands a little instead of shrinking, so the set mass presses against the mould and copies its surface.
common_mistakes: Writing that it shrinks on setting. It expands slightly, by about 1%.
Describing the hardening only. The slight expansion is what gives the sharp impression.
steps.memory_tip: Water back, hard mass, slight expansion of about 1%. Those three facts carry every use.
steps.margin_note: Name the slight expansion. It is the property the uses depend on.

steps.label: Where it is used
lines: Because it expands slightly, it takes
a sharp impression of a mould, so it
is used to make moulds and casts.

steps.why: Each use follows from the setting property. A hard mass that copies fine detail can hold a broken bone still and can reproduce the surface of a mould.
common_mistakes: Naming the plaster cast for bones only. The question asks for the importance, so the mould and statue uses belong here as well.
Listing uses with no reason. The hard set and the slight expansion are why it suits them.
steps.memory_tip: Moulds, bones, statues. All three need a hard set that copies fine detail.
steps.margin_note: Two or three named uses with the reason is a comfortable length.

insider_note: The property and the uses are one answer here: say that it sets to a hard mass and expands slightly, then name the uses that need exactly that.
